family_reason: Core is injecting local, global and third-party-library repository context into the prompt.
scope_reason: Repository-aware generation aimed at code reuse and conciseness; evaluated on generated functions.

family_reason: Candidates are checked by compiler/tests/timing and the result selects or drives revision.
scope_reason: Improves speed of LLM-generated assembly, measured by execution on tests.
gain_quote: the RL-trained model itself can still be improved with best-of-N sampling (i.e., from 1.46× in the single-sample setting to 1.93× with best-of-8 sampling).
gain_note: Headline is the best-of-8 selection component (8x samples); iterative-refinement numbers are only in figures.
core_idea: Sample several assembly rewrites and keep the fastest test-passing one, or revise using compiler, test and timing feedback.

family_reason: Main contribution is syntax-guided multi-task fine-tuning; compiler-filtered beam search is secondary.
scope_reason: Targets syntactic correctness of SQL-embedded code; readability is only a side human rating on CodeT5-base.
gain_quote: Lyra Reference CodeT5 TurduckenGen 3.152 (0.533) 3.492 (0.553)
gain_note: Table 9 column mapping is garbled in extraction (extraction reads 3.152 as CodeT5). Small human study (50 samples per dataset); pre-LLM-era model.
core_idea: Multi-task fine-tune with an auxiliary syntax-tree prediction task and filter beam candidates by compilation to produce valid embedded (turducken) code.

family_reason: Core is retrieving relevant past performance-fix knowledge into a zero-shot prompt.
scope_reason: LLM edits C# code to fix performance inefficiencies; evaluated on real fix instances.
gain_note: Efficiency judged by match to developer fixes, not measured runtime; top-100 of 100 samples per task.
core_idea: Retrieve a fix-specific prompt template from a knowledge base mined from past performance fixes and use it to prompt the model zero-shot.

family_reason: Title contribution is vulnerability-constrained decoding that forbids vulnerability-label tokens.
scope_reason: Aims to avoid vulnerabilities in auto-completed smart-contract code; evaluated on completions.
baseline_name: Fine-tuned GPT-J without vulnerability tuning or constrained decoding
gain_quote: Combined with the secure baseline percentage of 30%, our approach can increase the amount of secure code from 30% to 60%.
gain_note: 60% is chained from labeling and avoidance rates, not measured directly; about half of 'secure' outputs were whitespace only.
core_idea: Fine-tune the model to emit vulnerability labels with vulnerable code, then forbid those label tokens at decoding to steer away from vulnerable completions.

family_reason: Reinforcement learning (RRHF) with execution-based rewards on a small model.
scope_reason: Optimizes program speed; measured by execution on PIE.
gain_note: Single 60M model; CodeGen/Codex numbers copied from PIE, not head-to-head.
core_idea: Rank sampled candidate programs by compile, test and runtime outcomes and train the model with ranking-based RL (RRHF) on those rankings.

family_reason: Instruction tuning with masked NLL and unlikelihood loss on security data.
scope_reason: Targets security of generated code, measured with CodeQL.
baseline_name: StarCoder-1B with standard instruction tuning (w/o SafeCoder)
gain_quote: StarCoder-1B n/a w/o SafeCoder with SafeCoder 55.6 62.9 92.1
gain_note: One of six models shown; gains do not generalize to unseen CWEs.
core_idea: Jointly instruction-tune on normal data and vulnerability-fix pairs, raising likelihood of secure tokens and applying unlikelihood loss to vulnerable tokens.

family_reason: Model is re-prompted to revise its own code with generic CWE fix instructions; no external checker.
scope_reason: Prompting technique to make Copilot output more secure; judged on generated samples.
gain_quote: According to the results, the iterative method is the best-performing one to increase the number of secure solutions synthesized and reduce the number of insecure synthesized samples – the number of secure samples was increased by 8% in contrast to the baseline while the number of insecure samples was reduced by 12%.
gain_note: Quote gives the relative figure; 40 and 48 come from the garbled Table 1 (40%|...|48%). Only 25 samples per method; manual judgment.
core_idea: Iteratively re-prompt Copilot with ten generic 'Fix the CWE' instructions from MITRE's Research Concepts view.

family_reason: PPO reinforcement learning with runtime-based reward.
scope_reason: Targets runtime of generated HPC code; measured by execution.
gain_quote: We demonstrate that our finetuned model improves the expected speedup of generated code over base models for a set of benchmark tasks from 0.9 to 1.6 for serial code and 1.9 to 4.5 for OpenMP code.
gain_note: vs base model (weak baseline); OpenMP 1.9 to 4.5. Single base model.
core_idea: Fine-tune with PPO using rewards from measured runtimes plus a learned performance reward model.

family_reason: Role, chain-of-thought steps and few-shot examples in the prompt, no feedback.
scope_reason: Generates reusable API methods with better naming; evaluated on generated methods.
gain_metric: Method name expressiveness, average human rating (1-4)
gain_note: Column order Human / APIzator / Code2API; human-written APIs scored 3.39. Naming judged by humans only; input is human SO snippets.
core_idea: Prompt with a role, an eight-step chain of thought and five examples to turn Stack Overflow snippets into reusable, well-named API methods.

family_reason: Fine-tuning on a new kind of optimization-pair data.
scope_reason: Targets speed of optimized code; measured with gem5 execution.
gain_quote: leading to significant improvements in both optimization ratios (31.24% → 58.90%) and speedup (2.95×→5.22×).
gain_note: Same-model comparison of training data; anchor verification (other technique) adds more.
core_idea: Build training pairs from different users' solutions to the same problem (slow vs fast) instead of one user's successive revisions.

family_reason: Main novelty is retrieving HLS optimization strategies for in-context pragma insertion.
scope_reason: LLM generates and optimizes HLS C++ for FPGA runtime; borderline hardware domain.

gain_note: Speedup vs CPU software, not vs handcrafted HLS; per-kernel results vs handcrafted are mixed (worse on some). No aggregate vs handcrafted.
core_idea: Profile the program, split it into pipelined tasks, and retrieve HLS optimization strategies so the LLM inserts pragmas, followed by design-space exploration.

family_reason: Several specialized fine-tuned agents coordinated by an orchestration agent.
scope_reason: Readability only inside an aggregated survey score; implementation claims dubious.
gain_note: Paper reports only ranges: CortexCompile 'above 4.5' vs GPT-4o '3.5 to 4.2'; no exact pair. Readability not separable.

family_reason: Security model guides token probabilities of the target LLM during decoding.

family_reason: Dense retrieval of a secure demonstration inserted as in-context example.
scope_reason: Targets security of generated code, measured with CodeQL.

gain_note: Relative figure; unclear whether 7.20 is percentage points or relative. 12.07% vs no-technique LM.
core_idea: Retrieve a secure code demonstration with a dense retriever and prepend it as an in-context example.

family_reason: Preference optimization (DPO) on self-generated, self-validated data.

gain_note: Measured on commonly solved problems; same model without CodeDPO (no efficiency-specific baseline).
core_idea: Score self-generated code and tests with a PageRank-style mutual verification and add faster-vs-slower pairs, then train with DPO.

family_reason: Tree-based decoding that scores tokens by execution outcomes.
scope_reason: Decoding strategy targeting execution performance of generated code.
gain_quote: Comparative evaluations with leading large language models, such as CodeLlama and GPT-4, show that our framework achieves an average performance enhancement of nearly 30%.
gain_note: Abstract only; relative; 'nearly 30%' is approximate and baseline details unknown.
core_idea: Guide token selection with a code token tree whose node scores are updated from multi-objective execution results (correctness, performance, similarity).

family_reason: Static analysis (Pulse, ISL) result drives sanitizer insertion.
scope_reason: Sanitizer wraps client calls instead of improving generated code; no correctness check.
gain_metric: Share of provable manifest memory-safety bugs sanitised (%)
gain_note: Headline 'sanitises 100% of the bugs which do have a proof' has no baseline number; per-project counts in garbled tables.
core_idea: Use blame-carrying incorrectness separation logic to attribute memory-safety bugs to the generated function and insert sanitizers at call sites.

family_reason: Preference alignment (SimPO) on synthesized vulnerability-inducing data.
scope_reason: Targets vulnerability ratio of generated code via static analyzer.
baseline_name: Same model aligned with SafeCoder dataset
gain_quote: Specifically, the models aligned with P RO S EC are more secure than ones aligned with SafeCoder by 25.2% (33.47 v.s. 44.72) and 35.4% (26.04 v.s. 40.33).
gain_note: First of two models (Phi3-mini-Inst) shown.
core_idea: Synthesize CWE-guided instructions that induce vulnerable code, have the model fix them, and align on the resulting preference pairs with data selection.

family_reason: Tree search where execution and profiling results are fed back into self-critique.
scope_reason: Targets efficiency and correctness; runtime measured.
baseline_name: Average over baselines (CoT, Reflexion, LDB, Best-of-N, etc.)

family_reason: Domain-specific fine-tuning framework.
scope_reason: Abstract only; unclear if maintainability is measured; compared to human practice.
gain_note: Abstract gives no numbers; venue possibly predatory.

family_reason: Exploration, implementation and verification squads of LLM agents.

family_reason: Main components are retrieval-augmented editing and data augmentation in an agent.

family_reason: Supervised fine-tuning on a large decompilation dataset.

gain_note: Relative figure; ES is similarity to reference, a correctness proxy.

family_reason: Mined anti-pattern dictionary and embedding search locate and guide edits.

family_reason: Multi-agent framework with hardware optimization techniques.

gain_note: Abstract only; no numbers.

family_reason: LLM-chosen crossover inside a genetic-improvement search driven by execution fitness.

family_reason: Several LLMs independently optimize code, then search-based selection.

family_reason: Localized preference optimization on distilled preference data.

family_reason: Profiler-guided advisor-generator-evaluator loop.
scope_reason: LLM optimizes code for latency/energy; measured by execution.
gain_metric: Average relative latency improvement on DaCapo
gain_quote: On large-scale application codes, to which prior LLM approaches have not scaled, it surpasses compiler optimizations, achieving average relative improvements of 1.54× in latency (vs. 1.01× for the compiler) and 1.24× in energy (vs. 1.08× for the compiler).
gain_note: Edits existing code; LLM baseline (PerfCodeGen) used only on HumanEval.

family_reason: Main novelty is CV segmentation and page-transition graphs supplied in the prompt.

gain_note: Abstract only; no numbers for readability or maintainability.

family_reason: Curriculum policy optimization with EDA-based rewards.
scope_reason: Targets PPA of LLM-generated Verilog; hardware efficiency.
gain_quote: Our ChipSeek models achieve state-of-the-art results, with our best configuration improving functional correctness (pass@5) by 11.4% and reducing the worst, average and best EDAP by 20%, 18% and 9% respectively compared to the previous best-performing models.
gain_note: Relative figure; 'best configuration'.
core_idea: RL with curriculum-guided dynamic policy optimization and hierarchical rewards from EDA synthesis results.

family_reason: Contrastive RL (GRPO) training for CUDA optimization.
scope_reason: Targets CUDA kernel speed; measured by execution.

gain_note: Mean inflated by outliers (median 1.42); train/test overlap on KernelBench.
core_idea: Train with RL where the prompt includes previous kernels and their measured speedups so the model contrasts faster and slower variants.

family_reason: Meta-prompting generates context-aware optimization prompts.

core_idea: Use a meta-prompter LLM to write project-, task- and model-aware optimization prompts.

family_reason: Security knowledge graph retrieved into planning prompt.

gain_note: vs base model; RAG baseline numbers in garbled table; table shows 16 vs text 15.

gain_quote: As shown in Table 3, the multi-agent approach achieves higher performance speedup than the single-agent approach (1.32× vs. 1.08×), while both approaches consistently generate correct kernels.
gain_note: Only 3 kernels and one model.

family_reason: Model confirms and filters its own package recommendations.

gain_note: Original prompt 7.48%; single model (GPT-4o-mini).
core_idea: Ask the model in a chain of confirmation steps to verify that each recommended package exists before answering.

family_reason: Category-aware routing across generation, debugging and refinement agents.

gain_note: Speedups given per language (1.050-1.427x); best PCG baseline differs per language; no single aggregate pair.
core_idea: Route each problem to the models profiled as best for its algorithmic category across generation, debugging and refinement.

family_reason: Evolutionary search where compile/test/timing results guide next generations.

gain_quote: The EvoEngineer-Free configuration paired with Claude-Sonnet-4 achieves a median speedup of 2.72×, outperforming all competing approaches.

core_idea: Evolve kernels with an LLM using a two-layer design of solution guiding and prompt engineering plus population management.

family_reason: SFT then GRPO with execution-guided reward including time and memory.

family_reason: Plan, code and debug agents with tree search.

gain_note: Level 1 only; subset of KernelBench; single model.
core_idea: Multi-agent plan/code/debug team with grounded instructions, dynamic context windows and epsilon-greedy tree search.

family_reason: Coder and Judge agents with hardware profiler feedback.
